# Jubilees Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Division of the Earth; Canaan Seizes the Promised Land

---

**8:1** In the twenty-ninth jubilee, first week, first year, Arpachshad married Rasu'eja, daughter of Susan daughter of Elam. She bore him a son in the third year.

**8:2** He named the boy Kainam. As Kainam grew up, his father taught him to write. When he came of age he went exploring, looking for a place to settle and build himself a city.

**8:3** He came across an inscription carved into rock by people from before the flood. He read it, copied it down — and it led him into sin. The inscription preserved the Watchers' instructions for reading astronomical omens: how to interpret the movements of the sun, moon, and stars.

**8:4** He kept the whole thing secret. He was afraid of what Noah would say if he found out.

**8:5** In the thirtieth jubilee, second week, first year, he married Melka, daughter of Madai son of Japheth. In the fourth year she gave birth to Shelah.

**8:6** In the thirty-first jubilee, first week, second year, Shelah married Mu'ak, daughter of his uncle Kesed.

**8:7** She gave him a son named Eber. Eber later married 'Azurad, daughter of Nebrod, in the thirty-second jubilee, seventh week, third year.

**8:8** In the first year of the thirty-third jubilee she bore him a son he called Peleg — because in those very days, Noah's descendants were beginning to divide the earth among themselves. That is why: Peleg.

**8:9** They worked out the division among themselves privately and then presented it to Noah.

**8:10** So at the start of the thirty-third jubilee, the earth was formally divided into three parts for Shem, Ham, and Japheth, according to each one's inheritance — first year, first week — one of the angels was there to guide them.

**8:11** Noah called his sons and grandsons together. They gathered close, and he oversaw the lot-drawing for the three territorial portions. They each reached forward and pulled their lot from the fold of Noah's garment.

**8:12** Shem's lot: the middle of the earth, his permanent inheritance for all generations — beginning at the middle of the Rafa mountain range, at the headwaters of the Tina River, running west through that river's course until reaching the waters of the deep from which the river flows out into the Maat Sea and from there into the great ocean.

**8:13** Everything north of that line goes to Japheth. Everything south of it is Shem's.

**8:14** The boundary extends westward to Asshur's territory, then continues west to the western sea, running west until it reaches the sea of Ailt.

**8:15** From there it turns east through the sea of Girit, then east again to the Red Sea, then north to the sea of Girit, and north again to the Tina River.

**8:16** The sea here called the Red Sea lies between Atel and the great sea — extending to the Maat Sea and on to the sea of Girit.

**8:17** From the sea of Girit it runs west along the sea of Tirrin, back to the sea of Girit, and then east from Tirrin to the sea of Asshur.

**8:18** From there it reaches Mount Rafa on its north side — the northern boundary of Shem's portion.

**8:19** This entire region is Shem's heritage, to be held by him and his descendants forever: five great islands and a great land in the east.

**8:20** Ham's lot: beyond the Gihon River, southward to the right side of the Garden. It runs south through all the volcanic mountains, then west to the sea of Atel, and continues west until it reaches the sea of Mauk — the sea of no return, the sea from which nothing that enters ever emerges — until the day of final judgment when all who have corrupted their ways before God will face the reckoning.

**8:21** It runs north to the borders of Gadir and along the coastline of the sea.

**8:22** Japheth's lot: beyond the Tina River, north of its source, running northeast across all the territory of Gog and the entire eastern region.

**8:23** It continues far to the north, through the mountains of Qelt in the north, to the sea of Mauk, and east of Gadir as far as the coastline of the sea.

**8:24** This entire region is Japheth's heritage, to be held by him and his descendants forever: five great islands and a great land in the north.

**8:25** Climate tells you everything: Japheth's land is cold. Ham's land is hot. Shem's land sits in between — a blend of both.

**8:26** Ham's territory runs from the sea of Mauk all the way to the sea of Atel.

**8:27** Then Canaan looked across and saw the land of Lebanon — down to the Jordan and along the coast of the sea — and he simply took it. His father Ham, his brothers Mizraim, Put, and Cush watched and did nothing.

**8:28** Canaan settled in Lebanon from Hamath to the border of Egypt — he and his sons — and they have been there ever since.

**8:29** That is why the land of Canaan is under a curse and destined for servitude — because Canaan occupied the territory that belonged to Shem. The sons of Shem are obligated to drive him out as someone living under a curse, because that land is not Ham's portion. Everyone who has lived there under the name of Canaan has been living in wickedness.

**8:30** Ham knew his father had cursed Canaan, and he was deeply unhappy that Canaan had seized what belonged to Shem.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The Canaan land-seizure (vv.27-30) is the theological payoff — explaining Israel's right to Canaan as the restoration of Shem's territory. The "sea of no return" (v.20) is a striking Jubilees description of what may be the Atlantic or an outer cosmic sea. The three climate zones (v.25) provide an ancient ethnographic schema.*
